name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet and Russian chemist, pioneer of the 'framework' hypothesis and molecular layering (ML) method, founder of the scientific school 'Chemistry of highly organized substances'.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol’tsov
summary: Soviet and Russian chemist, co-founder of the molecular layering (ML) method, student and collaborator of V. B. Aleskovskii.

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
aliases: St. Petersburg State Technological Institute (Technical University)
summary: Oldest educational chemical engineering institute in Russia, where Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov developed the ML method.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: University where Aleskovskii later worked as rector and continued ML research.

name: Framework Hypothesis
summary: Hypothesis proposed by V. B. Aleskovskii in 1952, forming the theoretical basis for the molecular layering method.

name: Molecular Layering (ML) Method
summary: Gas-phase layer-by-layer deposition technique for synthesizing thin films, pioneered by Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov.

name: T. Suntola's 1974 Patent
summary: First patent on atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), filed by Tuomo Suntola in Finland with priority date November 29, 1974.

name: Department of Chemistry of Solids
summary: Department founded by V. B. Aleskovskii in 1967 at LTI by Lensovet, later renamed to Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials.

name: Department of Solid State Chemistry
summary: Department organized by V. B. Aleskovskii at Leningrad State University in 1977.

name: Virtual Project on the History of ALD (VPHA)
summary: International project initiated in 2013 to document the history of atomic layer deposition (ALD).

name: Mary, Turkmenistan
summary: Birthplace of Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii.

name: Proletarskaya Station, Rostov Region, USSR
summary: Birthplace of Stanislav Ivanovich Kol’tsov.

name: St. Petersburg, Russia
summary: City where Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov conducted their research and developed the ML method.

name: Naval Research Institute in Leningrad
summary: Institute where Aleskovskii worked as a research fellow after graduating from LTI by Lensovet.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: National academy of the Soviet Union, where Aleskovskii was elected a corresponding member in 1972.

name: Supreme Soviet of the Russian Federation
summary: Legislative body of the Russian Federation, where Aleskovskii served as a member.

name: Leningrad Scientific Center of the USSR Academy of Sciences
summary: Scientific center co-founded by Aleskovskii, later headed by Zhores I. Alferov.

name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist, pioneer of atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) and atomic layer deposition (ALD).

name: Riikka Puurunen
summary: Finnish scientist, leader of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD (VPHA).

name: Chemistry of Highly Organized Substances
summary: Scientific school founded and supervised by V. B. Aleskovskii.

name: Inter-University Scientific and Technical Program 'Chemical Assembly of Materials'
summary: Program founded in 1978 under Aleskovskii's supervision to advance ML research in the USSR.

name: Svetlana
summary: Leading USSR electronics engineering organization that collaborated with Aleskovskii on ML-made dielectric thin films.

name: Pravda Newspaper
summary: Leading Soviet newspaper where Aleskovskii published an article on chemical assembly in 1977.

name: Nikolai Aleksandrovich Kosygin
summary: Prime Minister of the USSR who took interest in Aleskovskii's work on molecular layering.

name: Zhores Ivanovich Alferov
summary: Nobel laureate and Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences, later head of the Leningrad Scientific Center.

name: Galina Nikolaevna Kuznetsova
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, defended candidate dissertation in 1965 on ML-related research.

name: Anna Nikolaevna Volkova
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, defended candidate dissertation in 1969 on ML-related research.

name: Galina Viktorovna Sveshnikova
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, defended candidate dissertation in 1971 on ML-related research.

name: Anatolii A. Malygin
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, co-author of the source document, and current head of the Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials.

name: Victor E. Drozd
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, co-author of the source document, and pioneer of vacuum ML equipment.

name: Vladimir M. Smirnov
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, co-author of the source document, and researcher in solid state chemistry.

name: Anatolii A. Malkov
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov, researcher in ML and co-author of the source document.

name: Dimitar Damyanov
summary: Bulgarian scientist who collaborated with Aleskovskii and Kol’tsov on ML research.

name: Robert Bruce Merrifield
summary: American chemist, Nobel Prize winner in 1984 for solid-phase peptide synthesis, whose work paralleled ML research.

name: Mstislav Vsevolodovich Keldysh
summary: President of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR who supported Aleskovskii's ML research for microelectronics.

name: Alexei P. Alekhin
summary: Director of the Research Institute of Physical Problems by N.F. Lukin and head of the Department of General Chemistry at MIPT.

name: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (State University)
summary: Leading Russian university where A. P. Alekhin headed the Department of General Chemistry.

name: Ferry Watt, LLC
summary: Russian vacuum equipment manufacturing company that developed ML/ALD thin film apparatus.

name: Chemical Assembly of Nanomaterials, LLC
summary: Company in Saint Petersburg, Russia, involved in the production of ML-based materials and equipment.

name: Svetlana-Roentgen
summary: Company that collaborated with Aleskovskii's school on producing ceramic insulators for X-ray tubes using ML technology.

name: ALD Conference in Helsinki (2014)
summary: International conference on atomic layer deposition held in Helsinki, Finland, in May 2014.

name: ALD Conference in Kyoto (2014)
summary: International conference on atomic layer deposition held in Kyoto, Japan, in June 2014.

name: 1st International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy (Espoo/Helsinki, 1990)
summary: First international symposium on atomic layer epitaxy, where V. E. Drozd presented on ML research in the USSR.

name: Stoichiometry and Synthesis of Solid Compounds
summary: Monograph by V. B. Aleskovskii published in 1976, laying out the theoretical foundations of the 'framework' hypothesis and ML method.

name: Chemistry of Solids
summary: Textbook by V. B. Aleskovskii published in 1978, based on his monograph and lecture notes.

name: Chemistry of Supramolecular Compounds
summary: Monograph by V. B. Aleskovskii published in 1996, expanding on his theories of solid-state chemistry.

name: Chemical-Informational Synthesis
summary: Textbook by V. B. Aleskovskii published in 1997, exploring theories of chemical synthesis and nanotechnology.

name: Silica Gel: Its Structure and Chemical Properties
summary: Monograph by S. I. Kol’tsov and V. B. Aleskovskii published in 1963, detailing early ML research.

name: Synthesis of Solids by the Molecular Layering Method
summary: Doctoral dissertation by S. I. Kol’tsov defended in 1971, defining the principles of the ML method.

name: Active Silica
summary: Candidate dissertation by V. B. Aleskovskii defended in 1940, focusing on silica research.

name: Framework Hypothesis and Experience the Preparation of Certain Active Catalysts
summary: Doctoral dissertation by V. B. Aleskovskii defended in 1952, introducing the 'framework' hypothesis.

name: The Study of Interaction of Carbon Tetrachloride with Silica Gel
summary: Candidate dissertation by S. I. Kol’tsov defended in 1963, marking the first phase of ML research.

name: IVS-1 Sorbent
summary: Industrial sorbent-indicator for water vapor, produced using ML technology.

name: FS-1-3 Sorbent
summary: Industrial sorbent for water vapor, amines, and organic compounds, produced using ML technology.

name: Ales-1 ML Unit
summary: Flow-vacuum ML unit for the manufacture of supercapacitor components, developed by SPbSTI and Chemical Assembly of Nanomaterials, LLC.
